result.title: From Single-Actor Environments to Multi-Actor Event Worlds: Can LLMs Be Event World Models?
result.summary: World models help agents assess the consequences of their actions before acting. Many real systems, however, involve multiple actors who make their own decisions, can evolve even when the agent takes no action, and are only partially observed through event logs. We formalize these systems as event worlds and ask whether large language models can predict future observations from the log and the agent's proposed actions. We build complementary benchmarks from human Diplomacy games and real Polymarket trades. Our hierarchical framework compares prediction with and without other actors' actions, then tests multi-step rollouts, predictions for actions never taken, and usefulness to agents. Fine-tuning and more data improve prediction when all actors' recorded actions are given. With only the agent's action, models struggle when other actors strongly affect the outcome, and larger models and longer histories help little. This gap also limits multi-step prediction and agent decisions, with models overestimating plan success. Yet imagined experience and initialization from world models can still improve policy learning. Anticipating other actors' actions remains a central challenge for event world modeling.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将多主体、部分可观测系统形式化为「事件世界」，用外交游戏与 Polymarket 数据构建基准，检验 LLM 能否根据事件日志和智能体拟采取动作预测未来观测，并评估多步展开与策略学习中的可用性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其世界模型式未来观测预测、多步 rollout 与「想象经验」训练，可能为 LVR 的预测工作区、状态更新及规划可靠性提供方法线索；但该工作无视觉模态，也未涉及 latent reasoning 机制，迁移性有待核查。
